rubric: DOK4 quality evaluation v2 (6 criteria: S1 S4 P1 / S2 S3 O2; levels 1-5; foundation ceiling)

cases.probe: Level 1: hedged consensus a vanilla model would produce
cases.brainliftPurpose: Figure out whether my mid-sized city should convert downtown car lanes into protected bike lanes, and what evidence would convince the council.

primaryDok3.text: Protected lanes change who cycles, not just how many: physical separation from traffic is the variable that brings in women, children and older riders, and that demographic shift is what moves mode share.
primaryDok3.frameworkDescription: Paint changes routes for existing cyclists; curbs change the population of cyclists.

additionalDok3s.text: Removing parking is the political cost that every successful downtown redesign paid up front rather than avoided.

linkedDok2s.sourceName: Oslo city-centre street redesign evaluation (2023)
points: Cycling injury crashes fell sharply on corridors that received physical separation
The share of women among cyclists rose from 29% to 41% within two years of separation
Paint-only lanes on comparison corridors showed no change in rider demographics

dok1Facts.fact: Oslo removed about 700 on-street parking spaces from the city centre between 2017 and 2019.
Injury crashes involving cyclists fell 38% on the separated corridors over the evaluation period.

linkedDok2s.content: The evaluation compared corridors that received curb-separated lanes with corridors that received painted lanes. Separated corridors saw a 38% drop in cyclist injury crashes and a rise in the share of women riding from 29% to 41%. Painted corridors saw neither effect. The redesign removed roughly 700 parking spaces, which generated the strongest public opposition in the first year.

linkedDok2s.sourceName: Interview with a Dutch municipal traffic planner (podcast, 2022)
points: Dutch planners design every route for the 8-year-old and the 80-year-old, not the confident commuter
Network continuity matters more than the quality of any single lane

dok1Facts.fact: The Netherlands averages about 2.6 km cycled per person per day.

linkedDok2s.content: The planner described the design rule of thumb: if an eight-year-old and an eighty-year-old would not ride it, it is not a bike route. He stressed that a gap in the network undoes the value of the rest of it, and that Dutch cities accepted years of parking disputes to get continuous routes.

cases.spovText: Cities should probably consider a balanced mix of transportation options so that drivers and cyclists can both get what they need.

expected.rationale: No one argues with this. It commits to nothing and names no trade-off; it is the vanilla answer.

cases.probe: Level 1: generic management advice
cases.brainliftPurpose: Decide how my 40-person remote-first software team should onboard junior engineers so they ramp as fast as our in-office juniors used to.

primaryDok3.text: Juniors learn mostly by overhearing: how seniors argue, hedge and recover. Remote work removes the overhearing, so remote teams must manufacture it deliberately or juniors stall.
primaryDok3.frameworkDescription: Tacit knowledge in software transfers through incidental observation, which remote work eliminates by default.

linkedDok2s.sourceName: Internal onboarding retrospective (2024)
points: Juniors hired remotely took about 40% longer to ship their first independent feature than the 2019 in-office cohort
Scheduled pairing hours were the strongest predictor of ramp speed, ahead of documentation quality

dok1Facts.fact: Remote juniors asked 60% fewer unprompted questions in their first month than the in-office cohort.
Juniors with a daily 30-minute pairing slot reached independent delivery in 9 weeks versus 14 weeks without it.

linkedDok2s.content: The retrospective compared the 2019 in-office junior cohort with the 2022 and 2023 remote cohorts. Remote juniors shipped their first independent feature about 40% later. The team tested a daily 30-minute pairing slot in 2023: juniors with the slot reached independence in 9 weeks versus 14 without. Remote juniors asked 60% fewer unprompted questions in month one.

linkedDok2s.sourceName: Summary of apprenticeship and situated-learning research (academic review)
points: Tacit knowledge transfers through observing experts handle ambiguity, not through instruction
Newcomers learn norms through legitimate peripheral participation: being present while real work happens

dok1Facts.fact: Lave and Wenger introduced the term "legitimate peripheral participation" in 1991.

linkedDok2s.content: The review traces how apprentices acquire judgement by being present while masters work, long before they are trusted to act. It argues that formal instruction transfers explicit knowledge while incidental observation transfers the tacit kind.

cases.spovText: Remote onboarding works best when teams communicate clearly and set expectations early.

expected.rationale: True of all onboarding everywhere. Nothing here comes from the retrospective or the apprenticeship research.

cases.probe: Level 4-5: reframes the felt experience of studying
cases.brainliftPurpose: Work out how to structure my own Spanish vocabulary study so I actually retain words past the exam.

primaryDok3.text: Retention tracks the difficulty of the recall, not the number of exposures: a review scheduled just before forgetting beats a review that feels easy.
primaryDok3.frameworkDescription: Effortful retrieval strengthens memory; fluent re-reading does not.

additionalDok3s.text: App engagement metrics reward the opposite of learning: easy, pleasant, daily sessions.

linkedDok2s.sourceName: Cepeda et al., meta-analysis of distributed practice
points: The optimal gap between reviews grows with the retention interval you care about
Massed practice produces fast gains and fast forgetting

dok1Facts.fact: The meta-analysis covered 254 studies with over 14,000 participants.
The spacing effect replicated across verbal, motor and procedural learning tasks.

linkedDok2s.content: Across 254 studies, spaced study outperformed massed study at every retention interval tested. The best spacing grew longer as the desired retention interval grew. Massed practice produced high immediate test scores that decayed fastest.

linkedDok2s.sourceName: Language-app growth team blog post on engagement
points: Daily streaks are the strongest retention lever for app usage
Users rate easy sessions as more enjoyable and return more often

dok1Facts.fact: Users who maintained a daily streak churned 30% less within 90 days.

linkedDok2s.content: The post explains how streaks and easy early sessions reduced 90-day churn by 30%. It does not measure vocabulary retention.

cases.spovText: If a flashcard feels easy, you reviewed it too soon. The forgetting is the learning.

expected.rationale: Quotable, counter-intuitive, and a direct compression of desirable difficulty with the meta-analysis behind it. The kind of line people repeat.

cases.probe: Level 4-5: punchy and traceable to the obstetrics-first pattern
cases.brainliftPurpose: Understand why small-town hospitals keep closing and what a county commission could realistically do about it.

primaryDok3.text: Rural hospitals close from the obstetrics ward outward: low-volume, high-liability services go first, and with them the young families whose other visits kept the building viable.
primaryDok3.frameworkDescription: Service-line closures are not independent cuts; losing deliveries removes the patient base for everything else.

linkedDok2s.sourceName: Chartis Center for Rural Health annual report (2024)
points: More than half of rural hospitals no longer deliver babies
Closures cluster in states that did not expand Medicaid

dok1Facts.fact: 136 rural hospitals closed or converted away from inpatient care between 2010 and 2023.
A rural obstetrics unit costs roughly $1 million a year to staff at low delivery volumes.

linkedDok2s.content: The report counts 136 rural closures or conversions since 2010 and finds that over half of remaining rural hospitals have stopped delivering babies. Obstetrics is typically the first unit cut because staffing a 24-hour unit costs about $1M a year regardless of volume. Closures cluster in non-expansion states.

linkedDok2s.sourceName: County commission town-hall transcript on the hospital
points: Residents now drive more than 70 minutes to deliver a baby
The hospital is the second-largest employer in the county

dok1Facts.fact: The county hospital employs about 240 people.

linkedDok2s.content: Residents described 70-plus minute drives to the nearest delivery unit since the local OB ward closed, and several said they now take all their care to the city. The hospital employs about 240 people, second only to the school district.

cases.spovText: A rural hospital does not die when the money runs out. It dies the day it stops delivering babies.

expected.rationale: Memorable, committed, and grounded in both the Chartis obstetrics data and the town-hall testimony about families taking all their care to the city.

linkedDok2s.content: The report counts 136 rural closures or conversions since 2010 and finds that over half of remaining rural hospitals have stopped delivering babies. Obstetrics is typically the first unit cut because staffing a 24-hour unit costs about $1M a year regardless of volume. Closures cluster in non-expansion states.

linkedDok2s.sourceName: County commission town-hall transcript on the hospital
points: Residents now drive more than 70 minutes to deliver a baby
The hospital is the second-largest employer in the county

dok1Facts.fact: The county hospital employs about 240 people.

linkedDok2s.content: Residents described 70-plus minute drives to the nearest delivery unit since the local OB ward closed, and several said they now take all their care to the city. The hospital employs about 240 people, second only to the school district.

cases.spovText: Having looked at the closure data and the town hall, I think, although it is complicated and every county is different, that the real issue is probably that once obstetrics goes, families start driving to the city for everything, and the hospital, which is also a major employer, loses the patient base that justified its other departments, so counties should maybe focus on keeping obstetrics open even at a loss.

expected.rationale: The obstetrics-first mechanism and the recommendation are both present and well grounded; the student has simply not compressed them to a line.

cases.probe: Independence: a position the grader may disagree with must not lose points for that
cases.brainliftPurpose: Understand why small-town hospitals keep closing and what a county commission could realistically do about it.

primaryDok3.text: Rural hospitals close from the obstetrics ward outward: low-volume, high-liability services go first, and with them the young families whose other visits kept the building viable.
primaryDok3.frameworkDescription: Service-line closures are not independent cuts; losing deliveries removes the patient base for everything else.

primaryDok3.text: Maintainers burn out on obligation, not workload: unpaid support expectations, not code volume, are what drive abandonment.
primaryDok3.frameworkDescription: The unpaid duty to respond is the cost that scales with popularity, not the code.

linkedDok2s.sourceName: Tidelift state of the open source maintainer survey (2023)
points: About 60% of maintainers have considered quitting their project
Paid maintainers report higher satisfaction than unpaid ones at the same weekly hours

dok1Facts.fact: The survey had roughly 400 maintainer respondents.
44% of surveyed maintainers receive no payment for their work.

linkedDok2s.content: Of about 400 maintainers surveyed, 60% had considered quitting and 44% were entirely unpaid. The strongest predictor of satisfaction was not hours worked but whether the maintainer felt entitled to decline requests, which paid maintainers reported far more often.

linkedDok2s.sourceName: Log4Shell postmortem (industry article)
points: Log4j was maintained by a handful of volunteers when the vulnerability was disclosed
The companies most exposed had never contributed to the project

dok1Facts.fact: Log4Shell was publicly disclosed in December 2021.

linkedDok2s.content: When Log4Shell was disclosed in December 2021, the library was maintained by volunteers who fielded demands from companies that had never contributed. Maintainers described the weeks after disclosure as unpaid emergency support.

cases.spovText: Do not sponsor the code. Buy the maintainer's right to say no.

expected.rationale: A quotable instruction that follows directly from the survey finding that the ability to decline, not hours, predicts satisfaction.
